source_row.rationale: Restless leg syndrome is characterized by an uncomfortable, uncontrollable urge to move the legs, typically worsening in the evening or during periods of rest/inactivity, and temporarily relieved by movement, distinct from vascular conditions like peripheral artery disease, which is more associated with pain during activity.
source_row.source_detail: RLS definition: urge to move, engendered by stillness, usually evening-predominant and relieved by movement; current AASM resource, accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A urinary tract infection causing dysuria without new neurologic deficits","B":"Cauda equina syndrome requiring immediate imaging and surgical evaluation","C":"Uncomplicated sciatica appropriate for routine conservative outpatient care","D":"Mechanical low-back pain appropriate for routine nonurgent follow-up care"}}
source_row.rationale: Saddle anesthesia, bilateral leg weakness, and new bowel/bladder dysfunction in the context of severe back pain are red flag symptoms of cauda equina syndrome, a surgical emergency caused by compression of the cauda equina nerve roots, requiring immediate evaluation (MRI) and often emergency surgical decompression to prevent permanent neurological damage.
source_row.source_detail: Cauda equina red flags: urinary/bowel dysfunction and saddle anesthesia require urgent recognition/evaluation; current 2025/2026 StatPearls edition, accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.stem: A client with severe lower back pain develops new saddle anesthesia (numbness in the perineal/buttock area), bilateral leg weakness, and new bowel/bladder dysfunction. The nurse should recognize this as a possible sign of:

source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use prealbumin alone as a reliable measure of short-term nutrition response","B":"Interpret prealbumin primarily as a marker affected by inflammation and illness","C":"Use prealbumin as a specific marker of total body protein and muscle stores","D":"Prefer prealbumin over clinical assessment because of its shorter half-life"}}
source_row.rationale: Prealbumin (transthyretin) is strongly affected by inflammation and illness. ASPEN advises that visceral proteins such as albumin and prealbumin should not be used as stand-alone nutrition markers or proxies for total body protein. Nutrition assessment should integrate clinical history, intake, weight/body-composition findings and the inflammatory context.
source_row.source_detail: Visceral Proteins: albumin/prealbumin are inflammation-responsive and should not be used as nutrition markers; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: ASPEN — Visceral Proteins terminology guidance

source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A normal fibrinogen value reliably excludes disseminated intravascular coagulation from consideration","B":"Fibrinogen must be profoundly reduced at presentation for disseminated intravascular coagulation","C":"Fibrinogen may fall with consumption, but a normal or elevated value does not exclude DIC","D":"Fibrinogen has no useful role when evaluating suspected disseminated intravascular coagulation"}}
source_row.rationale: DIC consumes platelets and coagulation factors, and fibrinogen can decrease as consumption progresses. However, fibrinogen is also an acute-phase reactant and may remain normal or elevated, especially earlier in the process. A normal fibrinogen value therefore does not exclude DIC; diagnosis relies on the clinical setting and a pattern of serial coagulation findings.
source_row.source_detail: Evaluation/pathophysiology: consumptive coagulopathy can reduce fibrinogen, but laboratory diagnosis uses a pattern and fibrinogen may not be low early; last update 2024, accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.rationale: AST and ALT are liver enzymes that are typically elevated in the setting of hepatocellular injury or inflammation (such as from hepatitis, medication toxicity, or other liver conditions), and significant elevation warrants further evaluation of liver function and the underlying cause.
source_row.source_detail: AST/ALT are markers of hepatocellular injury; last update June 8, 2026, accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A laboratory pattern unrelated to thyroid function or pituitary regulation","B":"Primary hypothyroidism with low free T4 and compensatory elevation of TSH","C":"Normal thyroid function despite abnormal free T4 and TSH concentrations","D":"Primary hyperthyroidism with excessive thyroid hormone and suppressed TSH"}}
source_row.rationale: A low free T4 combined with an elevated TSH is the classic laboratory pattern of primary hypothyroidism, in which the thyroid gland is underproducing thyroid hormone, prompting increased pituitary TSH secretion in an attempt to stimulate more hormone production.
source_row.source_detail: Elevated TSH with low free T4 indicates primary hypothyroidism; current patient/clinical education page, accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: American Thyroid Association — Thyroid Function Tests

source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A kidney-filtration marker that independently confirms or excludes sepsis","B":"An abnormal marker that may reflect hypoperfusion and should be trended in context","C":"A specific measure proving that tissue oxygen delivery has already improved","D":"A normal metabolic finding that has no relevance during sepsis resuscitation"}}
source_row.rationale: Serum lactate is used in sepsis assessment and resuscitation because elevation may accompany tissue hypoperfusion and physiologic stress. It is not specific for sepsis or anaerobic metabolism, and an isolated value cannot confirm or exclude sepsis. Elevated lactate should be trended when indicated and interpreted with the full clinical picture.
source_row.source_detail: Blood lactate/serial lactate recommendations: lactate may reflect impaired perfusion but is nonspecific and must be interpreted in clinical context; 2026 guideline, accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Arterial sampling better assesses oxygenation because PaO2 requires arterial blood","B":"Arterial sampling is used mainly for research rather than bedside oxygenation","C":"Venous sampling provides an equivalent PaO2 for routine oxygenation assessment","D":"Arterial sampling primarily measures glucose and electrolytes rather than gases"}}
source_row.rationale: Arterial blood gas sampling reflects oxygenated, post-pulmonary blood, providing an accurate assessment of oxygenation status (PaO2) in addition to acid-base status, whereas venous blood gas primarily reflects tissue metabolism and has more limited direct use for assessing oxygenation, though it can still provide useful acid-base and some metabolic information in certain clinical contexts.
source_row.source_detail: PaO2/oxygenation requires arterial sampling; updated 2026 StatPearls, accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.rationale: Best practice for administering multiple medications via a feeding tube includes giving each medication separately, with water flushes between each medication (and before/after the entire process), to prevent potential drug interactions or incompatibilities within the tube and to help maintain tube patency.
source_row.source_detail: Administer multiple medications separately and flush between each medication; Nursing Skills, accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Place the client flat in a supine position to reduce respiratory effort","B":"Place the client upright in High-Fowler position to support lung expansion","C":"Place the client prone with the head turned to limit chest wall movement","D":"Place the client in Trendelenburg position to increase diaphragmatic pressure"}}
source_row.rationale: High-Fowler's position (sitting the client upright, typically at 60-90 degrees) allows for maximal lung expansion by reducing pressure from abdominal organs on the diaphragm and optimizing chest wall movement, making it the preferred position for a client experiencing respiratory distress, unless otherwise contraindicated.
source_row.source_detail: High-Fowler/tripod positioning promotes chest expansion and reduces work of breathing; 2nd ed. 2024, accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.rationale: Correct oral suctioning technique involves applying suction intermittently, primarily during catheter withdrawal, limiting each pass to a brief duration to minimize mucosal trauma and hypoxia, and reassessing the client's respiratory status and secretion clearance between passes, repeating as needed.
source_row.source_detail: Apply suction intermittently during withdrawal; limit suction pass to 10–15 seconds and reassess; accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.rationale: For a client unable to get out of bed, the nurse uses the occupied bed-making technique, working from one side of the bed to the other, safely rolling the client (with assistance as needed) while maintaining the client's privacy, safety, comfort, and proper body mechanics for the nurse throughout the process.

source_row.rationale: The current final USPSTF recommendation (May 8, 2018; update in progress as of 2026-08-14) recommends individualized decision-making for PSA-based screening in men aged 55–69 after discussion of benefits and harms. It recommends against routine PSA-based screening in men aged 70 years or older.

source_row.rationale: The ABCDE mnemonic for skin self-exams teaches clients to check moles for: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation (multiple colors within one mole), Diameter greater than about 6mm, and Evolving characteristics (any change in size, shape, or color over time) — all warning signs that should prompt further evaluation by a healthcare provider.

source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Screen only newborns with a documented family history of childhood hearing loss","B":"Screen all newborns so hearing loss can be identified and addressed early","C":"Delay hearing screening until speech delay becomes apparent in early childhood","D":"Omit routine screening because congenital hearing loss is too uncommon to screen"}}
source_row.rationale: Routine newborn hearing screening (recommended for all infants, typically before hospital discharge) allows for early identification of hearing loss, which is important because timely intervention (before 6 months of age, when possible) significantly supports optimal speech, language, and cognitive development, given the critical early window for auditory-based learning.

source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Recurrent binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors such as purging","B":"Persistent caloric restriction without binge eating and with markedly low weight","C":"Occasional overeating during stress without recurrent compensatory behaviors","D":"Sustained food restriction causing low weight without recurrent binge episodes"}}
source_row.rationale: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (such as self-induced vomiting, laxative or diuretic misuse, fasting, or excessive exercise) to prevent weight gain, often occurring in individuals with a body weight in the normal or above-normal range, distinct from anorexia nervosa's pattern of restriction and low body weight.
source_row.source_detail: Diagnostic features include recurrent binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors; accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.rationale: Conduct disorder is characterized by a repetitive, persistent pattern of behavior in which the basic rights of others or major age-appropriate societal norms are violated, including aggression toward people or animals, destruction of property, deceitfulness or theft, and serious rule violations, distinguishing it from typical adolescent behavior variations.
